mainEntity.name: How does calibration and certification tracking work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every machine carries its own certification and calibration schedule with attached documents and automated renewal alerts, so nothing runs past its due date unnoticed. It supports the calibration of welding equipment under ISO 17662 and the equipment records expected by ISO 3834.

mainEntity.name: Can it trace consumables and filler metals by batch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Consumables are logged at batch level with storage and reheat rules and low-stock alerts, and heat numbers are captured, linked to their parent MTRs, and propagated down the project tree — so material traceability runs from goods-in to the finished weld.

mainEntity.name: Does the maintenance hub work from the floor?
Which standards does this help with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Equipment and consumable control underpins ISO 3834, EN 1090 and ASME IX, plus ISO 17662 for calibrating welding equipment. Elenchon keeps the underlying records attributed and locked as they are captured, so audit evidence is instant.

mainEntity.name: Is equipment management included in the Standard platform?
What is welding equipment management software?

acceptedAnswer.text: Welding equipment management software is the system that tracks the machines, tools and consumables on a fabrication floor and the records proving they're fit for use — calibration and certification status, maintenance history, and consumable batch traceability. Elenchon runs that whole register on-premise, so equipment evidence stays on hardware you own.
